memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: routine follow‑up of polycystic ovary syndrome, irritable bowel syndrome and chronic kidney disease.

PRESENTING COMPLAINT: She reports regular menstrual cycles on the combined oral contraceptive pill, occasional bloating and mild abdominal discomfort, and no edema or dyspnea on exertion.

EXAMINATION: BP 132/84 mmHg, weight 68 kg, height 1.58 m, BMI 27.2 (obese per Asian cut‑offs). Abdomen soft, non‑tender, no masses. Pedal pulses 2+ bilaterally.

IMPRESSION: PCOS well‑controlled on OC pill and metformin; IBS symptoms mild; CKD stage G3aA2 with eGFR 55 mL/min/1.73m2 and urine ACR 85 mg/g.

ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current medicines. Advise low‑salt diet, regular aerobic activity 150 min/week, and weight reduction target 5‑7%. Order fasting lipid profile, fasting blood sugar, HbA1c, serum testosterone, LH:FSH ratio, pelvic ultrasound, CBC, stool routine, tTG‑IgA, serum creatinine, eGFR, urine ACR and hemoglobin. Offer influenza vaccine today due to chronic kidney disease.

Return if: new chest pain, breathlessness >30 min, fever >39°C, worsening abdominal pain with vomiting, or sudden decrease in urine output.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Metformin 500 mg twice daily
Combined oral contraceptive pill (ethinylestradiol 0.03 mg + levonorgestrel 0.15 mg) once daily
Mebeverine 135 mg twice daily
Ispaghula husk 5 g once daily
Loperamide 2 mg as needed for diarrhoea (max 8 mg/24h)
Telmisartan 40 mg once daily
Dapagliflozin 10 mg once daily
Furosemide 20 mg once daily
Sodium bicarbonate 500 mg twice daily

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Fasting lipid profile: Total cholesterol 5.2 mmol/L (<5.2 borderline), LDL 3.0 mmol/L (<2.6 high), HDL 1.2 mmol/L (>1.0 normal), Triglycerides 1.8 mmol/L (<1.7 borderline).
Fasting blood sugar: 92 mg/dL (70‑99 normal).
HbA1c: 5.8% (4‑5.6 prediabetes).
Serum testosterone: 48 ng/dL (15‑70 normal female).
LH:FSH ratio: 1.8 (≤2 normal).
Pelvic ultrasound: Bilateral ovaries 9 ml volume, multiple follicles 2‑9 mm, no dominant cyst.
CBC: Hb 12.8 g/dL (12‑16), WBC 6.2×10⁹/L (4‑10), Platelets 210×10⁹/L (150‑400).
Stool routine: No ova, cysts or occult blood.
tTG‑IgA: Negative (<4 U/mL).
Serum creatinine: 1.2 mg/dL (0.6‑1.1 mild ↑).
eGFR: 55 mL/min/1.73m2 (≥60 normal).
Urine ACR: 85 mg/g (<30 normal ↑).
Hemoglobin: 12.8 g/dL (as above).

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: review of labs and blood pressure control.

PRESENTING COMPLAINT: She feels well, reports occasional bloating after meals, no dysuria or edema. Menstrual cycles regular.

EXAMINATION: BP 138/86 mmHg, weight 67 kg, BMI 26.8 (overweight). Abdomen soft, no tenderness. No pedal edema.

IMPRESSION: BP slightly elevated; LDL remains high; eGFR stable at 54 mL/min/1.73m2; urine ACR 78 mg/g. PCOS and IBS unchanged.

ARRANGEMENTS: Increase telmisartan to 80 mg OD to improve BP control. Continue other meds. Reinforce low‑salt (<5 g/d) and DASH diet, encourage brisk walking 30 min daily. Repeat serum creatinine, eGFR and urine ACR in 6 weeks.

Return if: headache, visual changes, chest pain, swelling of feet, or decrease in urine output.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: annual influenza vaccine and chronic disease review.

PRESENTING COMPLAINT: She denies fever, cough, or urinary symptoms. Reports good tolerance of meds, occasional mild bloating.

EXAMINATION: BP 130/82 mmHg, weight 66 kg, BMI 26.4 (overweight). Lungs clear, abdomen soft, no edema.

IMPRESSION: CKD stable (eGFR 52 mL/min/1.73m2, urine ACR 72 mg/g). PCOS controlled. IBS mild.

ARRANGEMENTS: Administered inactivated influenza vaccine (0.5 mL IM) today. Advise to continue low‑salt diet, regular exercise, and weight goal 62‑65 kg. Review in 3 months.

Return if: high fever >39°C, worsening cough with dyspnea, chest pain, or new urinary symptoms.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: increased bloating and loose stools over past 4 weeks.

PRESENTING COMPLAINT: She reports abdominal bloating after meals, 3‑4 loose stools per day, no blood or mucus. No weight loss.

EXAMINATION: BP 128/80 mmHg, weight 65.5 kg, BMI 26.2 (overweight). Abdomen mildly distended, hypoactive bowel sounds, no tenderness.

IMPRESSION: IBS‑D flare likely exacerbated by recent dietary changes and stress. CKD and PCOS unchanged.

ARRANGEMENTS: Start rifaximin 550 mg twice daily for 14 days. Continue loperamide PRN for diarrhoea. Advise low‑FODMAP diet trial, adequate hydration, and stress‑reduction techniques. Review symptoms in 2 weeks.

Return if: fever >38.5°C, bloody stools, severe abdominal pain, or vomiting preventing oral intake.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: routine 3‑month review after IBS treatment.

PRESENTING COMPLAINT: She reports bowel habit normalized to 1‑2 formed stools daily, bloating reduced. No urinary complaints.

EXAMINATION: BP 126/78 mmHg, weight 64.8 kg, BMI 25.9 (overweight). Abdomen soft, non‑tender.

IMPRESSION: IBS symptoms improved after rifaximin and low‑FODMAP diet. CKD stable (eGFR 50 mL/min/1.73m2, urine ACR 75 mg/g). PCOS unchanged.

ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current medicines. Reinforce low‑salt, low‑FODMAP as tolerated, and regular aerobic activity. Plan next review in 3 months.

Return if: new rectal bleeding, worsening abdominal pain with vomiting, fever >39°C, or sudden drop in urine output.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: 6‑month follow‑up of chronic conditions.

PRESENTING COMPLAINT: She feels well, reports regular menstrual cycles, no bloating, normal bowel movements, and no edema.

EXAMINATION: BP 124/76 mmHg, weight 64.2 kg, BMI 25.6 (overweight). Lungs clear, abdomen soft, no masses.

IMPRESSION: All three conditions stable. PCOS on OC pill and metformin; IBS in remission; CKD stage G3aA2 with eGFR 49 mL/min/1.73m2, urine ACR 70 mg/g.

ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current regimen. Encourage maintenance of weight 62‑65 kg, low‑salt diet, and annual influenza vaccine next autumn. Schedule next review in 4 months.

Return if: chest pain, breathlessness at rest, fever >39°C, severe abdominal pain, or decrease in urine output.
